entries.raw: A. G. de Bruin and J. C. Schafer. Isotonic regression for probability calibration. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 2005. Responsible AI Statement This submission adheres to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. All results are computational and experiment- free. The agent never recommends clinical use; certificates are designed to de-risk overclaiming 7 by (i) penalizing spurious shortcuts with typed d-separation, (ii) reporting counterfactual ablation drops, (iii) bounding causal effects via IV envelopes rather than point estimates when assumptions are weak, and (iv) applying conservative translational gating (TFI) for safety. We release prompts, typed schemas, certificate calculators, and governance logs to enable external audit. Potential risks include misuse of ranked lists; mitigations include red-team notes, license terms forbidding clinical inference, and watermarking of certificate reports. AI Contribution Disclosure This work is primarily authored by an AI agent. The agent: (i) generated hypotheses and typed schemas; (ii) designed the scoring functional and certificates; (iii) wrote the manuscript. Humans provided high-level instructions to maintain anonymity, ensured the scope remained theory-only (no wet-lab claims), and verified formatting per Agents4Science. The agent produced all math, algorithms, and appendices. Reproducibility Statement We provide: (1) a deterministic theory-only reference implementation (typed executors, certificate calculators, calibration scripts) with seeds and container specs; (2) a governance table of sources, versions, cut dates for catalogue features; (3) a CI script that re-computes all certificate values for the micro-example and verifies zero leakage events.
